# Lab notebook — every experiment, including the failures

Chronological record of what we tried, the actual numbers, and the verdict.
Negative results are kept deliberately: the honest value of the final result
depends on seeing the whole search, not just the winners.

**Source of truth is the code** — every row below is regenerated by the
command given. Numbers are from the runs on Binance data fetched Nov 2026
(BTC + 29 alts; PC1 index over 27 survivors). Expect small drift if data is
re-fetched later.

**Standing caveat (applies to every positive result):** the *design* (fields,
contrasts, the reversion idea, window grids) was chosen by RL + Claude while
watching PC1 hold-out numbers. Per-window params are honest (prior-year only),
but the pipeline has absorbed information through our choices. Nothing here is
"bankable" until a *frozen* design runs once on an untouched asset.

> **RESULT OF THE CLEAN TEST (§9): REFUTED.** The frozen design did NOT
> reproduce on untouched assets. The +77.9% PC1 headline (§8) is an artifact of
> tuning on PC1. Read §9 before trusting anything above it.

---

## 0. Comonad core — PASS
`cabal test golden` · `cabal test ols`
Reproduces every numeric trace in `aladdin/tape.tex` (heat + wave) and recovers
known OLS coefficients (max error 0.008, R² 0.99999). The machinery is correct.

## 1. Single-asset three readings (BTC, 2017–2026) — context
`cabal run comonad -- data/BTCUSDT.csv 180 20`

| strategy | total ret | Sharpe | maxDD | in-mkt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| buy & hold | +1670% | 0.80 | −83% | 100% |
| causal (live) | +379% | 0.71 | −54% | 25% |
| forecast (A), drift | +2521% | 0.92 | −68% | 66% |
| oracle (B), lookahead | ~3e19% | 10.5 | 0% | 51% |

Oracle is the perfect-foresight ceiling (meaningless magnitude). Causal's edge
is drawdown reduction, not return.

## 2. Forward model as OLS return-regression (Reading A) — **FAILED**
`cabal run fit`
Fitted law `Δp_{t+40} = +0.0067 + 0.227·v − 0.011·g − 0.024·a`, **R²(val) negative**.
Out-of-sample, forecast (A) underperformed the plain causal rule everywhere:

| cell | forecast(A) Sh | causal Sh | B&H Sh |
|---|---|---|---|
| TEST × in-time | 0.06 | 0.29 | 0.56 |
| TRAIN × holdout | −0.06 | −0.06 | −0.22 |
| TEST × holdout | −0.25 | +0.06 | −0.47 |

**Verdict:** the gap term `g` (the bookmaker thesis) has ~0 coefficient and
negative out-of-sample R². Predicting returns from the pool gap does not work.
The causal rule's value is regime-filtering (variance/drawdown), not forecasting.
*This was the first misread: forward map treated as the strategy, not the extrapolator.*

## 3. PCA of the universe — structural finding
`../venv/bin/python pca.py`
- PC1 = **62.5%** of variance (market factor, near-equal loadings).
- PC2 = 3.6% (new/DeFi: SOL, AAVE, FTM, UNI vs legacy BCH, DOGE, XLM, ETC).
- PC3 = 2.9% (metaverse: SAND +0.67, MANA +0.57).
- **Effective # independent factors (participation ratio) = 2.52.**

**Verdict:** the universe is ~1 asset + noise. By-coin hold-out is near-cosmetic
(all share PC1); the temporal hold-out carries the real independence. Honest
tuning budget ≈ 1–2 parameters. ⇒ run the strategy on PC1 itself.

## 4. PC1 index built
`../venv/bin/python pc1_index.py` → `data/PC1.csv`
27 survivors (dropped EOS/FTM/MATIC — delisted/migrated), 2214 days
2020-10-16 → 2026-11-07. Roughly flat-but-violent: the "trendless & violent"
regime the model is meant for.

## 5. Two-sided stencil on PC1, drift-only forward map (β=0) — diagnostic
`cabal run pc1` (first version)
Hold-out (2025-05→2026-11) B&H: −0.56 Sh / −55.8% / DD −71.6%. Causal trend: −0.61.

| config | walk Sh | ret | edge ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| p/curv (k10) | +0.57 | +26.5% | 2.17 |
| m/slope (k60) | +0.53 | +21.6% | 1.31 |
| g/slope (k60) | +0.43 | +15.2% | 0.56 |
| p/slope (k20) | −0.29 | −23.1% | 2.61 |
| m/curv, g/curv | ≈ −0.6 | — | ≤0.1 |

**Verdict:** with a drift forecast (deterministic in the past), every "two-sided"
walk rule is **causal in disguise** — algebra: `p/curv` reduces exactly to
"10-day momentum below 20-day momentum" (a pullback-buy). The future side was
redundant. Good causal functionals found; two-sided-ness not yet earning its keep.

## 6. Reversion-to-m forward map, β sweep on PC1 — **first real signal**
`cabal run pc1` (current version)

| config | β=0 holdout | β>0 holdout | β* |
|---|---|---|---|
| p/slope | −0.29 (−23%) | **+0.74 (+35%)** | 0.05 |
| p/curv | +0.57 (+26%) | **+0.75 (+32%)** | 0.02 |
| m/curv | −0.61 | +0.11 | 0.02 |
| m/slope | +0.53 | +0.47 | 0.05 |
| g/slope, g/curv | +0.43 / −0.64 | unchanged | 0 |

**Verdict:** injecting the volume-built pool price `m` (β>0) improved 4/6 configs
out-of-sample; p/slope flipped from losing to best. But confounded: β>0 pulls the
forecast toward `m`, which in a down market is below price ⇒ defensive. One bear
hold-out can't separate "m informative" from "β = defensiveness."

## 7. Multi-regime walk-forward — the confound test
`cabal run walkforward`
Nine 6-month hold-outs, 2022-07 → 2026-11, params selected on each prior year.

| config | BULL (4) Δ | bear (5) Δ | overall |
|---|---|---|---|
| **p/slope** | **+0.42, wins 3/4** | +0.89, 4/5 | −0.30→+0.38, 7/9 |
| p/curv | −0.27, 2/4 | +0.40, 3/5 | +0.40→+0.51, 5/9 |

**Verdict (preserve the disagreement):**
- **p/slope: reversion survives the bull test** — helps in up-regimes too, so `m`
  carries real information beyond defensiveness. The architecture's prediction holds.
- **p/curv: reversion only helps in bears, hurts in bulls** — here β *is* a
  defensiveness dial. Confound stands for this config.

## 8. Stitched out-of-sample bottom line (2022-07 → 2026-11, 1591 days)
`cabal run walkforward` (bottom-line section)

| | total ret | CAGR | Sharpe | maxDD | in-mkt | trades |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| market (B&H PC1) | −38.2% | −10.4% | 0.16 | −81.5% | 100% | 0 |
| two-sided, β=0 | −52.5% | −15.7% | −0.17 | −75.4% | 45% | 188 |
| **two-sided, reversion (p/slope)** | **+77.9%** | **+14.1%** | **0.53** | **−57.0%** | **33%** | 112 |
| two-sided, reversion (p/curv) | +58.0% | +11.1% | 0.47 | −60.9% | 30% | 57 |

**Verdict:** the validated rule beat a *losing* market (−38%) by ~116 points of
total return, with a third of the exposure and a quarter less drawdown — on an
honest walk-forward. The β=0→reversion swing (−52% → +78%) is the whole story.
**Not yet trustworthy** because: (a) design chosen while watching this data
(§standing caveat), (b) **zero transaction costs** (112 trades ≈ ~11% undeducted
drag at 0.1% round-trip), (c) one series / one asset class, (d) mild survivorship.

## 9. CLEAN TEST — frozen design on unseen assets — **REFUTED**
`cabal run walkforward -- oos/*.csv` and `oos/OOSPC1.csv`
Design frozen at commit 7b579f2. 8 Binance coins never in the universe, never in
the PCA, never seen (XTZ THETA HBAR ZIL BAT ENJ ZRX ICX), + a market factor built
from them (OOSPC1). Pre-registered hypothesis: p/slope + reversion beats both
buy&hold and β=0.

Individual coins (p/slope), mean Sharpe: market −0.08, β=0 **+0.08**, reversion **−0.09**; passed 3/8.
Unseen market factor OOSPC1 (p/slope): market −0.16, β=0 −0.10, reversion −0.01 (ret −51.5%, maxDD −87.5%).

**Verdict: REFUTED.** The +77.9% / Sharpe 0.53 of §8 did not reproduce on any
untouched asset. Reversion-to-m is the *worst* of the three on individual coins
and only trivially least-bad (still −51%) on a fresh market factor. β=0 — which
*lost* −52% on PC1 — is as good or better than reversion everywhere out-of-sample.
The ranking inverted: the signature of overfitting, not a shrunk-but-real effect.

What survived: the comonad framing is sound; the only durable property of the
bookmaker model across the whole project is drawdown/exit timing, not return
generation; reversion-to-m is NOT a validated edge. The harness correctly
falsified its own best result — that is the result.

**In dollars — $10,000 in, out-of-sample (2022-07 → 2026-11, zero costs):**

| $10k into… | ends at | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| strategy, unseen market factor (OOSPC1) | ~$4,850 | **lost ~$5,150** |
| strategy, equal split across the 8 unseen coins | ~$5,000 | **lost ~$5,000** |
| buy & hold, unseen market factor | ~$1,710 | lost ~$8,290 |
| buy & hold, 8 coins equally | ~$2,670 | lost ~$7,330 |
| *strategy on PC1 (overfit — do NOT believe)* | *$17,790* | *the mirage; gap to ~$5k is the overfit, priced* |

So out-of-sample you would have **lost about half** — but **less than buy & hold**
(which lost ~75-83%). That "win" is *pure drawdown-timing* (in cash ~half the time
during a crash), which the β=0 drift-only rule delivers just as well — it is NOT
the reversion edge, which was refuted. Losing less than a −80% market by sitting
out half of it is damage control, not an investment thesis. Costs would worsen all
strategy rows; outcome swings wildly by coin (HBAR +, BAT −94%).

---

## Open / next
- **Clean test done (§9) — refuted.** Do NOT present the PC1 +78% as a finding.
- Transaction costs never added (would only worsen everything).
- If pursued further: the honest unit is a *market factor* (not single coins),
  and any new idea must be pre-registered and tested on held-out assets BEFORE
  the numbers are seen — the one discipline that worked here.
- The bookmaker model's real, repeatable property (drawdown reduction) is worth
  studying on its own terms, separately from return-beating claims.
